title: Rovsing, Psoas and Obturator Signs in Suspected Appendicitis
subject: Eponyms
preview: Rovsing sign describes right lower quadrant pain provoked by left lower abdominal palpation.
quickRevision: Rovsing sign describes right lower quadrant pain provoked by left lower abdominal palpation.
Obturator sign may arise when a pelvic appendix irritates the obturator internus region.
These signs have limited sensitivity and must be combined with history, examination and imaging when indicated.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Rovsing sign describes right lower quadrant pain provoked by left lower abdominal palpation.
Psoas sign can reflect irritation involving the iliopsoas region, often with a retrocecal appendix.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Obturator sign may arise when a pelvic appendix irritates the obturator internus region.
These signs have limited sensitivity and must be combined with history, examination and imaging when indicated.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: The absence of these maneuvers does not exclude appendicitis.

quiz.question: Which sign is right lower quadrant pain elicited on left-sided abdominal palpation?
quiz.explanation: Rovsing sign describes right lower quadrant pain provoked by left lower abdominal palpation.
